- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.6) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly, especially after sharp spikes.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.3) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase forecast marginally, especially if recent prices are falling.
- Model frequently overshoots after strong upward sentiment spikes; apply a 5–10% downward correction to forecast peaks.
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust; introduce a “mean reversion” bias: reduce forecast by 2–5% for each negative sentiment day following a peak.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to lag behind true price movements by 2–5 days; adjust forecast to align with recent 7–14 day trend, not just 18-day history.
- When sentiment is flat (0.3–0.6) and price is trending, model often ignores momentum; add a small momentum multiplier (e.g., +0.5% per day of trend) to forecast if sentiment is neutral.
